title: fleetrc manifest
description: Where skills come from and which agents get them. Sources are listed in precedence order: the first source with a skill name wins.

extends.description: Team manifests, as paths or <repo>//<file> such as github:org/agents//team.json; a repository alone means its .fleetrc/manifest.json. They add sources only; their hooks, fleet, hub and report are ignored. An entry may be an object that leaves some of the team's skills or sources out; `fleetrc remove` writes it.

manifest.description: The team manifest, as a path or <repo>//<file>.

exclude.description: Skill names left out of every source the team manifest (and what it extends) declares.

excludeSources.description: Source ids of the team manifest left out.

agents.description: "all" for every agent installed on the machine (one whose folder is in your home, such as ~/.claude for Claude Code), or agent ids from the skills package (claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, opencode, cursor, github-copilot, ...). `fleetrc agents` lists the ids.

forks.description: Skills copied from upstream into the personal repository, by skill name. `fleetrc diff` and `merge` compare against `from` at `base`.

base.description: Upstream commit the fork was last merged with.

hooks.description: Commands run after a sync that changed matching files. Only the root manifest can declare them.

name.description: Names the hook in the report and in FLEETRC_HOOK. Defaults to run.

run.description: Shell command. Gets the sync report as JSON on stdin, FLEETRC_HOOK, and FLEETRC_CHANGED: the matched <source>:<file> lines.

on.description: <source id>:<glob> patterns, such as personal:pstack/**. Default: any change.

fleet.description: SSH hosts for `fleetrc fleet`, and tag:<name> entries that stand for every machine on your tailnet with that Tailscale tag.

hub.description: URL each sync POSTs its report to.

run.description: Shell command that gets the report JSON on stdin after each sync.

cron.description: When the timer runs the sync: a five-field cron expression (minute 0-59, hour 0-23, day of month 1-31, month 1-12, day of week 0-7), such as "*/30 * * * *". "* * * * *" runs it every minute. fleetrc refuses a value out of range when it reads the manifest.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the cron, such as "Europe/Madrid" or "UTC", or "local"; fleetrc refuses a name Node.js does not know. Defaults to "local": the machine's time zone, following its clock changes and a move to another zone. launchd and Task Scheduler run timers in the machine's time zone, so on macOS and Windows another zone works only when it gives the same times.

id.description: Names the source's folder in the state folder. Defaults to the repository, host or package name. Not a Windows device name such as con or aux, and unique without regard to case.

skills.description: Glob of skill folders inside the source, e.g. skills/*.

update.description: review: fetch and show a diff, apply only on `fleetrc update <source>`.

instructions.description: The user-level instruction file, linked as each agent's own (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, copilot-instructions.md). Its glob must match one file.

oneOf.description: Glob of files inside the source; it goes to every agent with an instruction file.
A glob of files inside the source for each agent id. Each agent gets its own files: nothing is translated.

subagents.description: Subagent files, linked into each agent's subagents folder (~/.claude/agents for Claude Code), keeping their folders below the glob's base.

oneOf.description: Glob of files inside the source; it goes to Claude Code only, since agents read other formats.
A glob of files inside the source for each agent id. Each agent gets its own files: nothing is translated.

commands.description: Command files, linked into each agent's commands folder (~/.claude/commands for Claude Code), keeping their folders below the glob's base.

oneOf.description: Glob of files inside the source; it goes to Claude Code only, since agents read other formats.
A glob of files inside the source for each agent id. Each agent gets its own files: nothing is translated.

mcp.description: A file inside the source holding {"mcpServers": {...}}, merged into every agent's MCP config (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Grok, OpenCode), each in its own format. Secrets are written as ${VAR}: a literal value in a header, or in an env key that looks like a token, key, secret, password or auth, fails that server. A server may list the agents it goes to in "agents". Only the root manifest can set it; an extended manifest's is ignored.

agentHooks.description: Hook definitions, in each agent's own hooks format: Claude Code's go into a plugin fleetrc writes at ~/.claude/skills/fleetrc, Codex's into ~/.codex/hooks.json (approve them in /hooks), Grok's into ~/.grok/hooks, Gemini CLI's into ~/.gemini/settings.json and Cursor's into ~/.cursor/hooks.json, each next to the user's own. Only the root manifest can set it; an extended manifest's is ignored.

oneOf.description: A file inside the source of Claude Code hooks, {"hooks": {...}}; it goes to Claude Code only.
A file inside the source for each agent id, in that agent's hooks format. Nothing is translated.
A git repository. With `path`, a working clone you edit, updated by fast-forward and linked in place; without, a copy fleetrc keeps.

git.description: owner/repo, github:owner/repo, or any git URL.

path.description: Working clone on this machine, e.g. ~/onmax/skills.

adopt.description: init, adopt and fork move hand-made skills into this source. Needs path.

followLinks.description: Follow links that lead out of the working clone, such as a dotfiles repository whose skills link into another repository of yours, to find and link skills. Without it they are left out, since a cloned repository's links come from whoever pushes to it. Only the root manifest can set it; an extended manifest's is ignored. Needs path.

oneOf.description: A site serving /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json (v0.2.0, with digests) or /.well-known/skills/index.json (v0.1).
A folder on this machine, linked in place.
